text: Over the last 30 days, several visitors expressed frustration with the timed-entry ticketing system, noting a lack of flexibility and difficulty accommodating changes or late arrivals. Some found the price high, especially for families, and felt the experience was crowded at times. There were also repeated criticisms about the use of AI in the exhibits, with some visitors feeling it detracted from learning about Theodore Roosevelt. Positive comments focused on the building’s architecture and interactive exhibits, but staff responsiveness and visitor flow received mixed feedback. Addressing ticketing policies and improving customer support could help reduce negative experiences.

windows.7: Over the past week, visitors have expressed frustration with the timed entry system, particularly the strict enforcement of reservations without flexibility or accommodation. Several reviews noted difficulties reaching customer service, with emails and calls going unanswered and the AI assistant failing to provide help. Staff interactions were described as unsympathetic or unhelpful, contributing to a negative experience. There were few comments on exhibits, and one mention suggested a need for improved staff training. Overall, the main issues relate to access policies and customer support.
